lake.source: a lake-sized basin; a default, not physics. It is a basin on the floor, not a shore

pond.source: a garden pond; a default, not physics

pool.source: Aaron's default for a pool: 5 m x 10 m x 2 m

sea.source: a sea-sized basin; a default, not physics. It is a basin on the floor, not an ocean

tank.source: a round tank; a default, not physics

g_earth.source: sigma_ground.field.interface.projectile.G_EARTH (the construct's own g comes from mentat/world/constants.lua)

density_kg_m3.source: the library has no body density; whole-body density of a person with partly inflated lungs is about 0.98-1.01 g/cm3 (Brozek/Siri body-composition literature); 985 is chosen so a person floats with the head just clear, which is the common experience

hull_hu.source: Source's standing player hull: 32 x 32 x 72 HU (0.61 x 0.61 x 1.37 m)

mass_kg.source: an adult; the engine's player mass is not used (swimmers are not rigid bodies here)

reach.source: a swimmer pulls themselves out at an edge when its top is no higher than their hands can reach overhead: the standing hull is 72 HU = 1.37 m; the climb itself is an affordance, not a force model

swim_thrust_n.source: sustained propulsive force of a recreational swimmer (order 100-200 N); with the hull's drag this gives about 0.6 m/s horizontal, which is slow for a swimmer: the hull's box area overstates a body's

freeboard_m.source: the wall stands this far above the water so it does not spill

max_bodies.source: water bodies at once on a server; a cap, not physics

max_bodies_per_tick.source: objects processed per physics tick across all water; a cap, not physics

max_footprint_m.source: longest side or diameter; a cap, not physics (the engine's world is about 16000 HU = 300 m across)

max_volume_m3.source: total water volume at once; a cap, not physics

min_footprint_m.source: shortest side or diameter; a cap, not physics

wall_m.source: thickness of the basin's walls and floor (collision shell)

ethanol.label: ethanol

heave_damping.source: wave-radiation damping of a floating body moving up and down, in the small-body limit (derived from the radiated power of a point source at the surface, Newman 1977 ch. 6; omega the body's own heave frequency sqrt(rho g A_w / m), k = omega^2 / g, A_w its waterplane area, T its draft). Without it a floater would ring for half a minute; with it, about three swings. Not in the library; the factor 1/2 should be confirmed. Heave only, deep-water radiation: a pool's walls reflect the real waves, this does not
heave_damping.value: b = 1/2 rho omega k A_w^2 exp(-2 k T)

refused_reason: the sigma-ground library has no density and viscosity for it, and I do not guess a liquid's properties; I have water, seawater, ethanol, glycerol and mercury

scale_law.source: gravity-regime cavity scaling for an impact of kinetic energy E in a liquid (crater radius ~ (E/rho g)^(1/4); Engel 1966, Gault); the prefactor 1 is an estimate. It sizes the DRAWN splash and ripple only: no fluid is simulated

dispersion.source: linear capillary-gravity waves (Kelvin 1871): deep water omega^2 = g k, shallow water c = sqrt(g d); g from the construct's world constants, sigma and rho from the liquid's own row
dispersion.value: omega^2 = (g k + sigma k^3 / rho) tanh(k d)

steepness.source: wave steepness a*k of each drawn component; the drawn waves are gentle: far below the Stokes limit a*k = 0.44 (H/lambda = 0.142, Michell 1893), so linear theory (the dispersion relation) is valid
